sec: Pre-renal vs ATN table & FeNa · p798

items.q: Match the urine output and albumin in the pre-renal vs ATN table — 1) Pre-renal AKI urine output  2) Pre-renal urine albumin  3) ATN urine albumin … A) (–) absent  B) ↓  C) Normal  D) 1+
items.exp: Table: pre-renal — urine output normal, urine albumin absent (–); ATN — urine output ↓, urine albumin 1+. (Book p798)

items.q: Urine microscopy shows muddy brown epithelial casts. According to the table this finding belongs to:
items.exp: Table: urine microscopy is (–) in pre-renal AKI and shows muddy brown epithelial casts in ATN. (Book p798)

items.q: The BUN/creatinine ratio in pre-renal AKI is:
items.exp: Table: BUN/creatinine ratio >20 in pre-renal AKI and <10 in ATN. (Book p798)

items.q: In the pre-renal vs ATN table, the urine sodium in ATN is:
items.exp: Table: urine Na⁺ <20 mEq/L in pre-renal AKI and >40 mEq/L in ATN. (Book p798)

items.q: Match urine creatinine and FeNa in the table — 1) Pre-renal urine creatinine  2) ATN urine creatinine  3) Pre-renal FeNa  4) ATN FeNa … A) <1%  B) <20  C) >2%  D) >40
items.exp: Table: urine creatinine >40 (pre-renal) versus <20 (ATN); FeNa <1% (pre-renal) versus >2% (ATN) — FeNa being marked as the best parameter. (Book p798)

items.q: The table marks FeNa as the best discriminator between pre-renal AKI and ATN.
opts: False — urine sodium is marked as best
False — the BUN/creatinine ratio is marked as best
False — no single parameter is marked
items.exp: In the table, FeNa carries the annotation '(Best)' — urine osmolality and specific gravity are normal in pre-renal AKI and ↓ in ATN, while urine pH is normal in pre-renal and rises in ATN. (Book p798)

items.q: Match urine osmolality, specific gravity and pH — 1) Pre-renal urine osmolality  2) ATN urine specific gravity  3) ATN urine pH … A) ↑  B) Normal  C) ↓
items.exp: Table: pre-renal — urine osmolality normal, specific gravity normal, pH normal; ATN — osmolality ↓, specific gravity ↓, pH ↑. (Book p798)

items.q: The treatment row of the pre-renal versus ATN table is:
opts: Fluids for pre-renal AKI and treatment of the cause for ATN
Dialysis for pre-renal AKI and fluids for ATN
Steroids for pre-renal AKI and diuretics for ATN
items.exp: Rx row: fluids for pre-renal AKI; Rx of cause for ATN. (Book p798)

items.q: Fill up: The formula for fractional excretion of sodium (FeNa) is (u.Na/u.Creatinine) × (______/S.Na).
items.exp: FeNa = (u. Na / u. Creatinine) × (S. Creatinine / S. Na); normal is 1–2%. (Book p798)

items.q: The normal value of FeNa is:
Why is FeNa reduced in pre-renal failure?
opts: Sodium reabsorption is increased (↓ urine Na) and creatinine secretion is increased (↑ urine creatinine)
Sodium reabsorption falls (↑ urine Na), while urine creatinine also falls
Both urine Na and urine creatinine fall, so the calculated ratio is unchanged
Aldosterone secretion is suppressed, so both urine Na and creatinine rise
items.exp: ↓FeNa in pre-renal failure occurs because Na⁺ reabsorption is increased (↓u.Na) and creatinine secretion is increased (↑u.Creatinine). (Book p798)

items.q: In which conditions can ATN show a FeNa below 1% because a pre-renal component predominates?
opts: Sepsis, urinary obstruction and acute interstitial nephritis
items.exp: ATN with FeNa <1: NSAIDs, rhabdomyolysis and contrast AKI, grouped because the pre-renal component is predominant. (Book p798)

items.q: All but one of the following favour ATN over pre-renal AKI. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Urine Na⁺ <20 mEq/L favours pre-renal AKI; muddy brown casts, BUN/creatinine <10 and FeNa >2% all favour ATN. (Book p798)
